(Kuang D-Y, Wei Y-F, Luo Y-S, Pei K-W, Cao Y-Y, Zhang M-F, Huang T-F, Pu L, Shi S-C 2025, Animals 15(18): 2745 (MDPI page opened from a search result; ASW cites it as redelimiting B. hengshanensis by naming Boulenophrys gutu)); the sex is therefore disputed and the value is not a reliable female value. Taxonomic Account; holotype printed 'HUNL 070600A, adult male') gives a different tympanum value for this specimen: '[...] tympanum diameter larger than half of eye diameter (EL 4.9, TYD 2.9), and equal to tympanum-eye distance (TYE 1.6); [...]', with TYD defined in its Methods as 'TYD largest horizontal tympanum diameter;' and the precision sentence 'Measurements were taken with a vernier caliper to the nearest 0.1 mm.' conditions: One specimen: holotype MHN-UCa-Am 1164, adult female, collected 24 October 2019 at Torre 4, Reserva Forestal Protectora Bosques de la CHEC, Manizales, Caldas, Colombia, 2730 m. Paratypes (n = 6: 3 females, 2 males, 1 indeterminate sex; MHN-UCa-Am 196, 198, 199, 1698, 1718, 1492) are not described for the tympanum in the sentence used. The preceding sentence of the Description of the Holotype ends '...supratympanic crest present, distinct, expanded laterally; pretympanic crest present.' Other tympanum statements in the paper agree (audit-1297, page reader): the Osteological description (Cranium) prints '[...] columella is present but reduced in size and articulated with the palatoquadrate and squamosal; tympanic annulus is absent [...]', Comparisons with other species print '[...] by the absence of the tympanum and annulus tympanic (present in those species).', and the Discussion links the absence of tympanic structures to reception of environmental vibrations (citing Castillo-Urbina et al. 2021). The middle-ear columella is therefore present but reduced; only the external tympanic structures are absent. Preserved museum specimen; anatomy only, hearing not tested.
